title: The Ark of the Covenant Vanished. 3 Answers
author: QUILL
notes: Aksum shown as a claim (Kebra Nagast, c. 14th c.). Mount Nebo/2 Maccabees added as tradition. Not-proven line in beat 10.

beats.text: Israel's holiest chest vanishes from the Bible.
Three answers exist. The last is the strangest.
Philistines capture it, then return it after seven months of plague.
beats.say: Philistines capture it, then return it after seven months of plague.

beats.text: Twenty years at Kiriath-jearim, then David brings it to Jerusalem.
beats.say: Twenty years at KIR-ee-ath-JEE-uh-rim, then David brings it to Jerusalem.
beats.label: 20 YEARS

beats.text: One: destroyed? Babylon burned the Temple, yet its loot list never names the Ark.
But Jeremiah 3:16 says it shall not come to mind.
beats.display: "Neither shall it come to mind" - Jeremiah 3:16

beats.text: Two: hidden. Second Maccabees says Jeremiah sealed it in a cave on Mount Nebo.
beats.say: Two: hidden. Second MAK-uh-beez says Jeremiah sealed it in a cave on Mount NEE-boh.

beats.text: Three, the strangest: the fourteenth-century Kebra Nagast says Solomon's son took it to Ethiopia.
beats.say: Three, the strangest: the fourteenth-century KEB-rah NAH-gahst says Solomon's son took it to Ethiopia.
beats.label: KEBRA NAGAST, c. 14TH CENTURY
beats.source: claim in the Kebra Nagast (c. 14th century)

beats.text: Today Ethiopia says it rests in a chapel in Aksum.
beats.say: Today Ethiopia says it rests in a chapel in AHK-soom.
beats.source: claim by the Ethiopian Orthodox tradition

beats.text: Not proven: it has never been shown publicly.
Shiloh, Nebo, Aksum: the trail goes cold.
beats.say: SHY-loh, NEE-boh, AHK-soom: the trail goes cold.

beats.text: Israel's holiest chest vanishes. Destroyed, hidden, or in Aksum?
beats.say: Israel's holiest chest vanishes. Destroyed, hidden, or in AHK-soom?

youtube.title: The Ark of the Covenant Vanished. 3 Answers 🗺️ #shorts
youtube.description:
Destroyed, hidden, or in Ethiopia? The Bible's trail ends in Jerusalem, and three answers fill the gap.
The Aksum story comes from the Kebra Nagast (c. 14th century), and the Ark has never been shown publicly. Claims are shown as claims.
#ArkOfTheCovenant #BibleHistory #Archaeology #MythUnearthed
